sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这里是《访谈》。

sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia Navarro.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚-纳瓦罗。

sentences.en: As one of the most popular websites in the world, Wikipedia helps define our common understanding of just about everything.
sentences.zh: 作为世界上最受欢迎的网站之一，维基百科帮助定义了我们对几乎所有事物的共同理解。

sentences.en: But recently, the site has gone from public utility to a favorite target of Elon Musk, congressional Republicans, and MAGA influencers, who all claim that Wikipedia is biased.
sentences.zh: 但最近，该网站已经从一个公共实用工具变成了埃隆·马斯克、国会共和党人以及MAGA意见领袖最喜欢的攻击目标，他们都声称维基百科有偏见。

sentences.en: In many ways, those debates over Wikipedia are a microcosm of bigger discussions we're having right now about consensus, civil disagreement, shared reality, truth, facts,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，围绕维基百科的这些争论正是我们现在正在进行的一系列更大讨论的缩影，关于共识、文明的意见分歧、共同的现实、真理、事实，

sentences.en: all those little easy topics.
sentences.zh: 所有这些轻松简单的小话题。

sentences.en: A bit of history.
sentences.zh: 一点历史。

sentences.en: Wikipedia was founded back in the Paleolithic era of the internet in 2001 by Larry Sanger and Jimmy Wales.
sentences.zh: 维基百科早在互联网的旧石器时代——2001年由拉里·桑格和吉米·威尔斯创立。

sentences.en: It was always operated as a non-profit and it employs a decentralized system of editing by volunteers, most of whom do so anonymously.
sentences.zh: 它一直作为非营利组织运营，并采用由志愿者组成的去中心化编辑系统，其中大多数人都是匿名参与的。

sentences.en: There are rules over how people should engage on the site, cordially, and how changes are made, transparently.
sentences.zh: 对于人们应该如何在网站上进行亲切的交流，以及如何透明地进行修改，都有相应的规则。

sentences.en: And it's led to a culture of civil disagreement that has made Wikipedia what some have called the last best place on the internet.
sentences.zh: 这催生了一种文明争论的文化，使维基百科成为了某些人所说的互联网上最后一块美好的净土。

sentences.en: Now, with that culture under threat,
sentences.zh: 如今，随着这种文化受到威胁，

sentences.en: Jimmy Wales has written a book called
sentences.zh: 吉米·威尔斯写了一本书，叫做

sentences.en: The Seven Rules of Trust, trying to take the lessons of Wikipedia's success and apply them to our increasingly partisan, trust-depleted world.
sentences.zh: 《信任的七条规则》，试图将维基百科成功的经验应用到我们这个日益党派化、信任匮乏的世界中。

sentences.en: And I have to say, I did come in skeptical of his prescriptions, but I left hoping he's right.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我一开始对他的处方持怀疑态度，但读完后我希望他是对的。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与维基百科联合创始人吉米·威尔斯的对话。

sentences.en: I wanted to talk to you because I think this is a very tenuous moment for truSt.
sentences.zh: 我想跟你聊聊，因为我觉得现在是信任非常脆弱的时刻。

sentences.en: And your new book is all about that.
sentences.zh: 你的新书正是关于这个主题的。

sentences.en: In it, you sort of lay out what you call the seven rules of trust based on your work at Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 在书中，你根据自己在维基百科的工作经验，梳理出了你所谓的信任七条规则。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about all those as well as some of the threats and challenges to Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 我们将会探讨所有这些规则，以及维基百科面临的一些威胁和挑战。

sentences.en: But big picture, how would you describe our current trust deficit?
sentences.zh: 但从宏观来看，你将我们当前的信任赤字描述为什么样的状况？

sentences.en: it?
sentences.zh: 它是什么样的？

sentences.en: I think I draw a distinction between what's going on maybe with politics and journalism, the culture wars and all of that, and day-to-day life.
sentences.zh: 我认为我将政治、新闻、文化战争等正在发生的事情与日常生活区分开来。

sentences.en: Because I think in day-to-day life, people still do trust each other.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为在日常生活中，人们依然互相信任。

sentences.en: People generally think most people are basically nice.
sentences.zh: 人们通常认为大多数人本性善良。

sentences.en: And we're all human beings bumping along on the planet trying to do our beSt. And obviously, there are definitely people who aren't trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 我们都是在这个星球上磕磕绊绊、努力做到最好的普通人。当然，也确实有不可信的人。

sentences.en: But the crisis we see in politics, trust in politicians, trust in journalism, trust in business, that is coming from other places and is something that we can fix.
sentences.zh: 但我们在政治中看到的危机——对政客的信任、对新闻业的信任、对商业的信任——那是由其他原因造成的，而且是我们能够修复的。

sentences.en: One of the reasons why you can be an authority on this is because you created something that scores very high on truSt. You have built something that people
sentences.zh: 你能成为这方面的权威的原因之一，是因为你创造了一个在信任度上得分极高、人们

sentences.en: sort of want to engage with.
sentences.zh: 愿意与之互动的平台。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I do think Wikipedia isn't as good as I want it to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我的确认为维基百科还没有达到我想要的那么好。

sentences.en: And so I think that's part of why people do have a certain amount of trust for us, because we try to be really transparent.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这也是人们对我们保持一定信任的原因之一，因为我们努力做到真正透明。

sentences.en: You know, you see the notice at the top of the page, sometimes it says the neutrality of this page has been disputed, or the following section doesn't cite any sources.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你会看到页面顶部的提示，有时上面写着“本页面的中立性受到争议”，或者“以下部分没有引述任何来源”。

sentences.en: people like that.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Not many places these days will tell you, hey, we're not so sure here.
sentences.zh: 如今没多少地方会告诉你：“嘿，我们这儿也不太确定。”

sentences.en: And it shows that the public does have a real desire for unbiased, sort of neutral information.
sentences.zh: 这表明公众确实对公正的、某种程度上中立的信息有着真正的渴望。

sentences.en: They want to truSt. They want the sources.
sentences.zh: 他们想要信任。他们想要来源。

sentences.en: They want you to prove what you're saying and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你证明你所说的话，诸如此类。

sentences.en: How does Wikipedia define a fact?
sentences.zh: 维基百科是如何定义事实的？

sentences.en: basically we're very old-fashioned about this sort of thing what we look for is good quality
sentences.zh: 基本上我们在这种事情上非常老派，我们寻找的是高质量的

sentences.en: sources so we we like peer-reviewed scientific research for example as opposed to populist
sentences.zh: 来源，例如我们喜欢同行评审的科学研究，而不是民粹主义的

sentences.en: tabloid reports you know we look for quality magazines newspapers etc so we don't typically treat a random tweet as a fact.
sentences.zh: 小报报道，你知道的，我们寻找优质的杂志、报纸等等，所以我们通常不会把一条随机的推文当作事实。

sentences.en: And so we're pretty boring on that regard.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上我们相当古板。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's sort of like the publication that you cite gets cited by other reputable sources that it issues corrections when it gets things wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就好比你引用的出版物会被其他信誉良好的来源所引用，而且当它出错时会发布更正。

sentences.en: It's all the old fashioned sort of good stuff.
sentences.zh: 这都是那些老派的好东西。

sentences.en: And I think it's important to say when we look at different sources, they will often come to things from a different perspective or different
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有一点很重要，那就是当我们查看不同的来源时，它们通常会从不同的视角或不同的

sentences.en: political point of view, that doesn't diminish the quality of the source.
sentences.zh: 政治观点来看待事物，但这并不降低该来源的质量。

sentences.en: So, for example, I live here in London in the UK.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我住在英国伦敦。

sentences.en: We have The Telegraph, which is a generally right-leaning, but quality newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我们有《每日电讯报》，它通常偏右，但是一份优质报纸。

sentences.en: We have The Guardian, generally left-leaning, but quality newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我们有《卫报》，通常偏左，但也是一份优质报纸。

sentences.en: Hopefully, the facts, as you read the articles and you glean through it, the facts should be reliable and solid.
sentences.zh: 希望当你阅读文章并仔细甄别时，其中的事实应该是可靠且扎实的。

sentences.en: But you have to be very careful as an editor to tease out, okay, what are the facts that are agreed upon here?
sentences.zh: 但作为一名编辑，你必须非常小心地挑拣出：好吧，这里达成共识的事实是什么？

sentences.en: And what are the things that are opinions on those facts?
sentences.zh: 而基于这些事实的观点又是什么？

sentences.en: And that's, you know, that's an editorial job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是编辑的工作。

sentences.en: It's never perfect and it's never easy.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会完美，也绝非易事。

sentences.en: And Wikipedia also is famously open source.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，维基百科也是开源的。

sentences.en: It's decentralized and essentially it's run by thousands of volunteer editors.
sentences.zh: 它是去中心化的，本质上由成千上万的志愿编辑运营。

sentences.en: You don't run Wikipedia, we should say.
sentences.zh: 我们应该说明一下，你并不运营维基百科。

sentences.en: It runs me.
sentences.zh: 是它在运营我。

sentences.en: How do those editors fix disputes when they don't agree on what facts to be included or on how something is written?
sentences.zh: 当这些编辑在应该包含哪些事实或如何撰写某事意见不一时，他们是如何解决争议的？

sentences.en: How do you negotiate those differences?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何协调这些分歧的？

sentences.en: Well, in the best cases, what happens and what should happen always is take a controversial issue like abortion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在最好的情况下，正在发生以及应该一直发生的情况是，以一个像堕胎这样有争议的议题为例。

sentences.en: Obviously, if you think about a kind and thoughtful
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你想到一个心地善良且体贴的

sentences.en: Catholic priest and a kind and thoughtful
sentences.zh: 天主教神父和一个心地善良且体贴的

sentences.en: Planned Parenthood activist, they're never going to agree about abortion, but probably they can come together because I said they're kind and thoughtful
sentences.zh: 计划生育行动主义者，他们在堕胎问题上永远不会达成一致，但他们或许能够走到一起——因为我说过他们心地善良且体贴——

sentences.en: and say, okay, but we can report on the dispute.
sentences.zh: 然后说，好吧，我们可以报道这场争议。

sentences.en: So, rather than trying to say abortion is a sin or abortion is a human right, you could say Catholic Church position is this and the critics have responded thusly.
sentences.zh: 因此，与其试图断言“堕胎是罪恶”或“堕胎是人权”，你不如说“天主教堂的立场是这样的，而批评者的回应则是那样的”。

sentences.en: You'll start to hear a little of the Wikipedia style because I believe that that's what a reader really wants.
sentences.zh: 你开始能听到一点维基百科的风格了，因为我相信这才是读者真正想要的。

sentences.en: They don't want to come and get one side of the story.
sentences.zh: 他们不想来这里只听故事的一面之词。

sentences.en: They want to come and say, okay, wait, hold on.
sentences.zh: 他们想来这里说：好吧，等等，稍等。

sentences.en: I actually want to understand what people are arguing about.
sentences.zh: 我其实想了解人们到底在争论什么。

sentences.en: I want to understand both sides.
sentences.zh: 我想了解双方的观点。

sentences.en: What are the best arguments here?
sentences.zh: 这里最好的论点是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And basically every page has what's called a talk tab where you can see the history of the discussions and the disputes, which relates to another principle of the site, which is
sentences.zh: 基本上每个页面都有一个所谓的“讨论”标签，你可以在那里查看讨论和争议的历史，这与网站的另一个原则息息相关，那就是

sentences.en: transparency.
sentences.zh: 透明度。

sentences.en: You can look at everything and see who did what and what their reasoning was.
sentences.zh: 你可以查看所有内容，了解谁做了什么以及他们的理由是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So, you know, oftentimes if you see something repeating, you think, huh, okay, well, why does it say that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，很多时候如果你看到某些内容反复出现，你会想：嗯，好吧，为什么会这么写？

sentences.en: Often you'll be able to go on the talk page and read sort of what the debate was and how it was, and you can weigh in there, and you can join in and say,
sentences.zh: 通常你将能够进入讨论页面，阅读当时的辩论情况以及它是如何处理的，你可以在那里发表意见，加入讨论并说：

sentences.en: oh, actually, I still think you've got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 哦，实际上，我觉得你们还是搞错了。

sentences.en: Here's some more sources.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些更多的来源。

sentences.en: Here's some more information.
sentences.zh: 这里有更多的信息。

sentences.en: Maybe propose a compromise, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 也许可以提出一个妥协方案，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And in my experience, it turns out that a lot of pretty ideological people on either side are actually more comfortable doing that because they feel confident in their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，事实证明，双方许多相当具有意识形态色彩的人实际上更乐意这样做，因为他们对自己的信念充满信心。

sentences.en: I think it's the people who, and you'll find lots of them on Twitter, for example, they're not that confident in their own values and their own belief system.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些——比如你在推特上能找到大量的这种人——对他们自己的价值观和信仰体系并不是那么有信心。

sentences.en: And they feel fear or panic or anger if someone's disagreeing with them rather than saying, huh, OK, look, that's different from what I think.
sentences.zh: 当有人不同意他们的观点时，他们感到的不是“嗯，好吧，看，那和我想的不一样”，而是感到恐惧、恐慌或愤怒。

sentences.en: Let me explain my position, which is where your more intellectually grounded person will come from.
sentences.zh: “让我解释一下我的立场”，这才是你更有智识基础的人会做的事。

sentences.en: What you're saying is supported actually by a study about Wikipedia that came out in the science journal Nature in 2019.
sentences.zh: 你所说的话其实得到了2019年发表在科学期刊《自然》杂志上的一项关于维基百科的研究的支持。

sentences.en: It's called The Wisdom of Polarized Crowds.
sentences.zh: 它名为《两极分化人群的智慧》。

sentences.en: Perhaps counterintuitively, it says that politically contentious Wikipedia pages end up being of higher quality,
sentences.zh: 也许与直觉相反，它指出政治上有争议的维基百科页面最终质量更高，

sentences.en: meaning that they're more evidence-based, they have more consensus around them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们有更多的证据支持，周围有更多的共识。

sentences.en: But I do want to ask about the times when consensus building isn't necessarily easy as it relates to specific topics on Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想问问关于建立共识并不一定容易的时候，当它涉及到维基百科上的特定主题时。

sentences.en: Some pages, they have actually restricted editing privileges.
sentences.zh: 有些页面实际上限制了编辑权限。

sentences.en: So So the Arab-Israeli conflict, climate change, abortion, unsurprising topics there.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿拉伯-以色列冲突、气候变化、堕胎，这些都是意料之中的主题。

sentences.en: Why are those restricted and why doesn't the wisdom of polarized crowds work for those subjects?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些主题会被限制？为什么两极分化人群的智慧对这些主题不管用？

sentences.en: Well, typically the subjects that are restricted are we try to keep that as short as we can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通常受到限制的主题——我们会尽量保持这种限制尽可能少。

sentences.en: The most common type of case is if something's really big in the news or if some big online influencer says, ah, Wikipedia is wrong, go and do something about it.
sentences.zh: 最常见的情况是，如果某个话题在新闻中非常重大，或者某个大型网络意见领袖说：“啊，维基百科错了，大家去搞点动静出来。”

sentences.en: And, you know, we get a rush of people who don't understand our culture, don't understand the rules, and they're just vandalizing, or they're just sort of being rude,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我们会迎来一波不了解我们的文化、不了解规则的人，他们只是在搞破坏，或者只是表现得粗鲁，

sentences.en: and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And we just, as a calming down, just like, okay, hold on, just slow down, we're going to protect the page.
sentences.zh: 为了让事态平静下来，我们就会想：好吧，等等，慢下来，我们要保护这个页面。

sentences.en: And then there are pages where, you know, the most common type of protection we call semi-protection, which just means you have to have had an account for,
sentences.zh: 然后有些页面，你知道的，最常见的保护类型我们称之为半保护，这只意味着你必须拥有一个账号达到——

sentences.en: I forget the exact numbers, it's something like four days, and you have made 10 edits without getting banned.
sentences.zh: 我忘了具体数字了，大概是四天左右，并且在没有被封禁的情况下进行了10次编辑。

sentences.en: Now, typically, and this is what's surprising to a lot of people about Wikipedia, like 99% of the pages, maybe more than 99%,
sentences.zh: 现在，通常来说——这也是让很多人对维基百科感到惊奇的地方——大约99%的页面，甚至可能超过99%，

sentences.en: you can edit without even logging in and it goes live instantly.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要登录就可以编辑，并且它会即时生效。

sentences.en: That's like mind-boggling.
sentences.zh: 这简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: But it kind of points to the fact that most people are basically nice.
sentences.zh: 但这某种程度上表明了这样一个事实：大多数人本性善良。

sentences.en: Most people are trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都是值得信赖的。

sentences.en: People don't just come by and vandalize Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 人们不会无缘无故地跑来破坏维基百科。

sentences.en: And often if they do, it's because they're just experimenting or they didn't believe that would – they're like, oh my God, it actually went live.
sentences.zh: 通常如果他们这样做了，是因为他们只是在做实验，或者他们不相信它会——他们会说：“哦天哪，它居然真的发布了。”

sentences.en: And I didn't know I was going to do that.
sentences.zh: “我不知道我会这么做。”

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, please don't do that again.
sentences.zh: 这就好像：是的，请不要再那样做了。

sentences.en: This brings me to some of the challenges.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了其中的一些挑战。

sentences.en: Wikipedia, while it has created this very trustworthy system, it is under attack from a lot of different places.
sentences.zh: 维基百科在创建了这个高度可信的系统的同时，正受到来自许多不同地方的攻击。

sentences.en: And one of Wikipedia's sort of superpowers can also be seen as a vulnerability, right?
sentences.zh: 维基百科的某种超能力也可以被看作是一种脆弱性，对吧？

sentences.en: The fact that it is created by human editors.
sentences.zh: 那就是它是由人类编辑创建的这一事实。

sentences.en: And human editors can be threatened, even though they're supposed to be anonymous.
sentences.zh: 而人类编辑可能会受到威胁，尽管他们本应是匿名的。

sentences.en: You've had editors doxxed, pressured by governments to doctor information.
sentences.zh: 你们曾有编辑遭到人肉搜索（doxed），受到各国政府施压以篡改信息。

sentences.en: Some have had to flee their home countries.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至不得不逃离祖国。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of what's happened in Russia, in India, where those governments have really taken aim at Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 我想到了在俄罗斯、在印度发生的事情，那些国家的政府确实把维基百科作为了打击目标。

sentences.en: Would you say this is an expanding problem?
sentences.zh: 你会说这是一个日益严重的问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会这么说。

sentences.en: I think that we are seeing all around the world a rise of authoritarian impulses towards censorship, towards controlling information.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在世界各地都看到针对审查制度、针对控制信息的威权冲动的抬头。

sentences.en: And very often these come, you know, as a wolf in sheep's clothing because it's all about protecting the children or whatever it might be that, you know,
sentences.zh: 很多时候，这些出现时，你知道的，披着羊皮，因为这全都是为了保护儿童或诸如此类的名义，你知道的，

sentences.en: you move forward in these kind of control ways.
sentences.zh: 你以这些控制性的方式推进。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, the Wikipedians are very resilient and they're very brave.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你知道的，维基百科人非常有韧性，也非常勇敢。

sentences.en: And one of the things that we believe is that in many, many cases, what's happened is a real lack of understanding by politicians and leaders of how Wikipedia works.
sentences.zh: 我们坚信的一点是，在许许多多的情况下，发生的事情实际上是政客和领导层对维基百科的运作方式缺乏真正的理解。

sentences.en: A lot of people really have a very odd assumption that it's somehow controlled by the Wikimedia Foundation, which is the charity that I set up that owns and operates the website.
sentences.zh: 很多人确实有一个非常奇怪的假设，认为它某种程度上是由维基媒体基金会控制的——这是我建立的拥有和运营该网站的慈善机构。

sentences.en: Therefore, they think it's possible to pressure us in ways that it's actually not possible to pressure us.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们认为有可能以实际上根本不可能的方式向我们施压。

sentences.en: The community has real intellectual independence.
sentences.zh: 这个社群拥有真正的智识独立性。

sentences.en: But yeah, I do worry about it.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我确实对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: I mean, it's always something that weighs very heavily on us is is volunteers who are in dangerous circumstances and how do they remain safe is like critically important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总有一些事情让我们感到非常沉重，那就是身处危险环境中的志愿者们，以及他们如何确保自身安全，这绝对是至关重要的。

sentences.en: I want to bring up something that just happened here in the US.
sentences.zh: 我想提出一件刚刚在美国这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: In August, James Comer and Nancy Mace, two Republican representatives from the House Oversight Committee, wrote a letter to Wikimedia requesting records, communication,
sentences.zh: 8月份，众议院监督委员会的两位共和党众议员詹姆斯·科默和南希·梅斯致信维基媒体，要求提供有关特定编辑的记录、通信、

sentences.en: analysis on specific editors and also any reviews on bias regarding the state of Israel in particular.
sentences.zh: 分析，以及任何关于以色列国相关的偏见审查。

sentences.en: their reason, and I'm going to quote here, is because they are investigating the efforts of foreign operations and individuals at academic institutions subsidized by U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们的理由是——我在这里引用原话——因为他们正在调查外国行动以及受美国纳税人资助的学术机构中的个人影响美国

sentences.en: taxpayer dollars to influence U.S.
sentences.zh: 的努力。

sentences.en: public opinion.
sentences.zh: 公众舆论。

sentences.en: So can you tell me your reaction to that query?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能告诉我你对那个问题的反应吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we've given a response to the parts of that that were reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我们已经对其中合理的部分做出了回应。

sentences.en: I mean, we what we feel like is there's a deep misunderstanding or lack of understanding
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们觉得大家对维基百科的运作方式存在深刻的误解或缺乏了解，

sentences.en: about how Wikipedia works you know ultimately the idea that something being biased is a proper and
sentences.zh: 归根结底，认为某种东西带有偏见就适合成为国会调查的合理对象，

sentences.en: fit subject for a congressional investigation is frankly absurd and so you know in terms of
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这是荒谬的，所以你知道的，就提出那些神神秘秘之类的问题而言，

sentences.en: asking questions about cloak and dagger whatever we're not going to have anything useful to tell them.
sentences.zh: 我们没有什么有用的信息可以告诉他们。

sentences.en: I'm like, I know the Wikipedians, they're like a bunch of nice geeks.
sentences.zh: 我觉得吧，我认识那些维基百科人，他们就像是一群可爱的好小伙。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, the
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，

sentences.en: Heritage Foundation here in the United States, which was the architect of Project 2025, have said that they want to dox your editors.
sentences.zh: 美国传统基金会（Project 2025 的幕后推手）曾表示，他们想要人肉搜索你们的编辑。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you protect people from that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你们如何保护人们免受这种伤害？

sentences.en: I mean, it's embarrassing for the Heritage Foundation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让传统基金会感到尴尬。

sentences.en: I remember when they were intellectually respectable.
sentences.zh: 我记得他们曾经在知识界备受尊敬。

sentences.en: And that's a shame that if that's what they think is the right way forward, they're just badly mistaken.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是他们认为正确的方向，那真是太遗憾了，他们大错特错了。

sentences.en: But it does seem that there is this movement on the right to target
sentences.zh: 但右翼确实似乎有一股针对维基百科的运动，

sentences.en: Wikipedia over these types of concerns.
sentences.zh: 起因正是这类担忧。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering why you think that's happening.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为这背后的原因是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难说。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different motivations, a lot of different people.
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的动机，也有很多不同的人。

sentences.en: Some of it would be, you know, genuine concern if they see that maybe Wikipedia is biased.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分可能是，你知道的，如果他们看到维基百科可能存在偏见，便会产生真正的担忧。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I have seen, for example, Elon Musk has said, Wikipedia is biased because
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我看到过，比如埃隆·马斯克曾说过，维基百科有偏见，因为

sentences.en: they have this really strong rules about only citing mainstream media and the mainstream media is biased.
sentences.zh: 他们有一套非常严格的规则，只引用主流媒体，而主流媒体本身就是有偏见的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an interesting question, interesting criticism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个有趣的问题，也是一个有趣的批评。

sentences.en: Certainly,
sentences.zh: 当然，

sentences.en: I think worthy of some reflection by everyone, the media and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我认为这值得每个人反思，包括媒体等等。

sentences.en: But it's hardly, you know, it's hardly news to anybody and not actually that interesting.
sentences.zh: 但这很难算是什么新鲜事，对任何人来说都不算，其实也没那么有趣。

sentences.en: Then other people, you know, in various places around the world, not speaking just of the U.S., but, you know, facts are threatening.
sentences.zh: 然后其他人，你知道的，在世界各地不同的地方，不仅仅指美国，事实是具有威胁性的。

sentences.en: And if you and your policies are at odds with the facts, then you may find it very uncomfortable for people to simply explain the facts.
sentences.zh: 如果你和你的政策与事实相左，那么当人们只是在阐述事实时，你可能会觉得非常难受。

sentences.en: And I don't know, that's always going to be a difficulty.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这总会是一个难题。

sentences.en: But we're not about to say, gee, you know, maybe science isn't valid after all.
sentences.zh: 但我们不会去说，天哪，你知道的，也许科学终究是不成立的。

sentences.en: Maybe the COVID vaccine killed half the population.
sentences.zh: 也许新冠疫苗杀死了半数人口。

sentences.en: No, it didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: Like, that's crazy and we're not going to print that.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了，我们不会刊登这种言论。

sentences.en: And so they're going to have to get over it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须接受现实。

sentences.en: I want to talk about a recent example of a controversy surrounding
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈最近关于维基百科的一个争议实例，

sentences.en: Wikipedia, and that's the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 那就是查理·柯克的遇刺。

sentences.en: You know, Senator Mike Lee called Wikipedia wicked because of the way it had described Kirk on its page as a far-right conspiracy theorist
sentences.zh: 你知道的，参议员迈克·李称维基百科居心不良，因为它的页面将柯克描述为极右翼阴谋论者，

sentences.en: among other complaints that they had about the page.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他们对该页面还有其他一些抱怨。

sentences.en: And I went to look at the time that we're speaking, and that description is now gone from Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 我在我们交谈的这个时间去查看了一下，那个描述现在已经从维基百科上消失了。

sentences.en: Those on the left would say that that description was accurate.
sentences.zh: 左翼人士会说那个描述是准确的。

sentences.en: Those on the right would say that that description was biased all along.
sentences.zh: 右翼人士则会说这个描述一直都带有偏见。

sentences.en: How do you see that, that tension?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待这种紧张关系？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think the correct answer is you have to address all of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我认为正确的答案是，你必须全面看待这一切。

sentences.en: You have to say, look, this was a person, I think the least controversial thing you could say about Charlie Kirk is that he was controversial.
sentences.zh: 你必须说，看吧，这是一个人物，关于查理·柯克，我认为最没有争议的说法就是他充满了争议。

sentences.en: I don't think anybody would dispute that.
sentences.zh: 我想没有人会对此提出异议。

sentences.en: And to say, like, okay, this was a figure who was a great hero to many people and treated as a demon by others.
sentences.zh: 并且要说，好吧，这是一个对许多人来说是伟大英雄，却被其他人视为恶魔的人物。

sentences.en: He had these views, many of which are out of step with, say, mainstream scientific thinking, many of which are very much in step with religious thinking and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他持有这些观点，其中许多观点与主流科学思维格格不入，但也有许多观点非常符合宗教思维，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And those are the kinds of things that if we do our job well, which I think we have in this case, we're going to describe all of that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把工作做好（我认为我们在这次事件中做到了），这些就是我们要去全面描述的内容。

sentences.en: Like maybe you don't know anything about Charlie Kirk.
sentences.zh: 就像你可能对查理·柯克一无所知。

sentences.en: You just heard, oh, my God, this man was assassinated.
sentences.zh: 你只是听说，天哪，这个人被暗杀了。

sentences.en: Who was it?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: What's this all about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, you should come and learn all that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你应该来这里了解这一切。

sentences.en: You should learn like who his supporters were and why they supported him and what are the arguments he put forward and what are the things he said that upset people.
sentences.zh: 你应该去了解谁是他的支持者，他们为什么支持他，他提出了什么观点，以及他说过哪些让人们感到不安的话。

sentences.en: That's just part of learning what the world is about.
sentences.zh: 这只是了解这个世界的一部分。

sentences.en: So those words that were there, far right and conspiracy theorists, those were, in your view, the wrong words and that the critics of Wikipedia had a point.
sentences.zh: 所以，之前在那里的那些词——极右翼和阴谋论者，在你看来，用词是不对的，维基百科的批评者有他们的道理。

sentences.en: Well, it depends on the specific criticism.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于具体的批评是什么。

sentences.en: So if the criticism is this word appeared on this page for 17 minutes, I'm like, you know what, you've got to understand how Wikipedia works.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果批评是某个词在这个页面上出现了 17 分钟，我会觉得，你知道吗，你得理解维基百科是如何运作的。

sentences.en: It's a process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个过程。

sentences.en: It's a discourse.
sentences.zh: 这是一场话语。

sentences.en: It's a dialogue.
sentences.zh: 这是一场对话。

sentences.en: But to the extent that he was called a conspiracy theorist by prominent people, that's part of his history.
sentences.zh: 但就他被知名人士称为阴谋论者而言，那是他生平的一部分。

sentences.en: That's part of what's there.
sentences.zh: 那是其中客观存在的一部分。

sentences.en: And Wikipedia shouldn't necessarily call him that.
sentences.zh: 维基百科不一定非要叫他阴谋论者。

sentences.en: But we should definitely document all of that.
sentences.zh: 但我们绝对应该把所有这些都记录下来。

sentences.en: You mentioned Elon Musk, who's come after Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 你提到了埃隆·马斯克，他一直在找维基百科的麻烦。

sentences.en: He calls it Wokipedia.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“觉醒百科”（Wokipedia）。

sentences.en: He's now trying to start his own version of Wikipedia called Grokipedia.
sentences.zh: 他现在正试图推出他自己的维基百科版本，叫做“Grokipedia”。

sentences.en: And he says it's going to strip out ideological bias.
sentences.zh: 他说这将剥离意识形态的偏见。

sentences.en: I wonder what you think attacks like his do for people's trust in your platform writ large.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为他这样的攻击会对人们对你们这个平台的整体信任产生什么影响。

sentences.en: Because as we've seen in the journalism space, if enough outside actors are telling people not to trust something, they won't.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在新闻领域所看到的，如果有足够多的外部行动者告诉人们不要信任某样东西，他们就不会信任了。

sentences.en: Well, you know, it's very hard to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这很难说。

sentences.en: I mean, I think for many people, their level of trust in Elon Musk is extremely low because he says wild things all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为对很多人来说，他们对埃隆·马斯克的信任度极低，因为他满嘴跑火车。

sentences.en: So to that extent, you know, when he attacks us, people donate more money.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种程度上，你知道的，当他攻击我们时，人们反而捐了更多的钱。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's not my favorite way of raising money.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这不是我最喜欢的筹款方式。

sentences.en: But the truth is, a lot of people are responding very negatively to that behavior.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，很多人对这种行为做出了非常负面的反应。

sentences.en: One of the things I do say in the book, and I've said to Elon Musk, is that type of attack is counterproductive, even if you agree with Elon Musk.
sentences.zh: 我在书中说过，我也对埃隆·马斯克说过，这种攻击适得其反，即使你同意埃隆·马斯克的观点。

sentences.en: Because to the extent that he has convinced people falsely that Wikipedia has been taken over by woke activists, then two things happen.
sentences.zh: 因为在他错误地让人们相信维基百科已被觉醒激进分子接管的程度上，接下来会发生两件事。

sentences.en: You're kind and thoughtful conservatives who we very much welcome, and we want more people
sentences.zh: 你们这些善良而有思想的保守派——我们非常欢迎你们，我们需要更多思想深邃、有知性、

sentences.en: who are thoughtful and intellectual and maybe disagree about various aspects of the spirit of our times.
sentences.zh: 或许对我们时代精神的各个方面持有不同看法的人。

sentences.en: Come and join us, and let's make Wikipedia better.
sentences.zh: 请来加入我们，让我们把维基百科做得更好。

sentences.en: But if those people think, oh, no, it's just going to be a bunch of crazy woke activists, they're going to go away.
sentences.zh: 但如果这些人认为，哦，不，这里只剩下一群疯狂的觉醒激进分子了，他们就会离开。

sentences.en: And then on the other side, the crazy woke activists are going to be like, great, I found my home.
sentences.zh: 然后另一边，那些疯狂的觉醒激进分子就会觉得，太好了，我找到归宿了。

sentences.en: I don't have to worry about whatever.
sentences.zh: 我不用再担心什么了。

sentences.en: I can come and write rants against the things I hate in the world.
sentences.zh: 我可以来这里长篇大论地抨击我讨厌的世界。

sentences.en: We don't really want them either.
sentences.zh: 我们其实也不欢迎他们。

sentences.en: You said you talked to Elon Musk about this.
sentences.zh: 你说你跟埃隆·马斯克谈过这事。

sentences.en: When did you talk to him about it?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候跟他谈的？

sentences.en: And what was that conversation like?
sentences.zh: 那次对话是怎样的？

sentences.en: I mean, we've had various conversations over the years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些年来我们有过各种各样的对话。

sentences.en: You know, he texts me sometimes, I text him sometimes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有时他给我发短信，有时我给他发短信。

sentences.en: He's much more respectful and quiet in private.
sentences.zh: 他在私底下要尊重得多，也安静得多。

sentences.en: But that you would expect,
sentences.zh: 但这也是意料之中的，

sentences.en: It's got a big public persona.
sentences.zh: 他有一个很大的公众人设。

sentences.en: When was the last time you had that exchange?
sentences.zh: 你们上次交流是什么时候？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think the morning after the last election, he texted me that morning.
sentences.zh: 我想是上次大选结束后的那天早晨，他那天早上给我发了短信。

sentences.en: I congratulated him.
sentences.zh: 我祝贺了他。

sentences.en: Obviously, the debate that happened more recently was because of the hand gesture that he made that was interpreted in different ways.
sentences.zh: 显然，最近发生的争论是因为他做了一个手势，被人们以不同的方式解读了，

sentences.en: and he was upset in the way that it had been characterized on Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 而他对这个手势在维基百科上的描述方式感到不满。

sentences.en: Yeah, I heard from him after that.
sentences.zh: 是的，在那之后我收到了他的消息。

sentences.en: I mean, in that case, I pushed back because I went to check like, oh, what does Wikipedia say?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种情况下我进行了回击，因为我去查了一下，哦，维基百科上是怎么写的？

sentences.en: And it was very matter of fact.
sentences.zh: 结果非常客观。

sentences.en: It said he made this gesture, it got a lot of news coverage, many interpreted it as this, and he denied that it was a Nazi salute.
sentences.zh: 上面说他做了这个手势，获得了大量新闻报道，许多人将其解读为这样，而他否认这是纳粹礼。

sentences.en: That's the whole story.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个故事。

sentences.en: It's part of history.
sentences.zh: 这是历史的一部分。

sentences.en: I don't see how you could be upset about it being presented in that way.

sentences.en: You get to a certain age in life, you're going through, you've got ambitions, you've got great dreams, and everything's fine.
sentences.zh: 当你到了生命的某个阶段，你经历着这一切，你有雄心壮志，有伟大的梦想，一切都很好。

sentences.en: And there on the distant hill is death.
sentences.zh: 而远处的山冈上就是死亡。

sentences.en: And you think, well, now is the time to wake up and live.
sentences.zh: 你会想，好吧，现在是醒来并好好生活的时候了。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权力斗争中。
